q: 1. The cement becomes useless if it absorbed moisture more than
explain: When cement absorbs moisture beyond about 5%, hydration begins prematurely inside the bag, forming lumps and losing its binding strength, making it unfit for use.

q: 2. The workability of concrete is defined as the
options: ease with which it can be mixed, transported and placed in position in a homogeneous state
breaking up of cohesion in a mass of concrete
separation of water or water-cement mixture from the freshly mixed concrete
explain: Workability describes how easily fresh concrete can be mixed, transported, placed, and compacted without segregation, while remaining homogeneous.

q: 3. Segregation in concrete results in
explain: Segregation separates coarse aggregate, mortar, and water unevenly, which can cause honeycombing, porous layers, and surface scaling all at once depending on where separation occurs.

q: 4. Harshness in concrete is due to the excess of
explain: An excess of coarser particles relative to fines reduces the paste's ability to lubricate the mix, making the concrete harsh and difficult to work.

q: 5. Ferro-concrete is another name given to (Ferror = iron)
explain: Ferro-concrete literally means iron-concrete, referring to concrete reinforced with steel (iron) bars, i.e., reinforced cement concrete.

q: 6. Reinforced cement concrete is equally strong in taking
explain: By combining concrete (strong in compression) with steel reinforcement (strong in tension) and proper detailing for shear, RCC is designed to resist tensile, compressive, and shear stresses effectively.

q: 7. The cement concrete in which high compressive stressed are artificially induced before its actual use, is called
explain: Prestressed concrete has internal compressive stresses artificially induced (via tensioned tendons) before loading, so that tensile stresses from service loads are offset.

q: 8. The cement concrete, from which entrained air and excess water are removed after placing it in position, is called
explain: In vacuum concrete, a vacuum process is applied after placing to remove excess water and entrapped air, increasing density and early strength.

q: 9. The sound absorption coefficient of light weight concrete is nearly ......than that of ordinary concrete.
explain: The porous structure of light weight concrete gives it roughly twice the sound absorption coefficient compared to dense ordinary concrete.

q: 10. In making precast structural units for partition and wall lining purposes, the concrete should be
explain: Light-weight concrete is preferred for precast partition and lining units because it reduces dead load while still providing adequate strength and insulation.

q: 11. The characteristic, which makes the concrete a versatile and widely used material of modern construction, is the possibility of
options: controlling the properties of concrete by using appropriate ingredients
molding the concrete in any desired shape
complete mechanization of concrete preparation and its placing process
explain: Concrete's versatility comes from a combination of factors: controllable properties through mix design, moldability into any shape, and full mechanization of production and placement, all of which together make it widely used.

q: 12. A suitable admixture added at the time of preparing the concrete mix, makes the concrete
explain: Different admixtures are available to impart different properties, so depending on the admixture chosen, concrete can be made water-proof, acid-proof, or of higher strength.

q: 13. The function of aggregates in concrete is to serve as
explain: Aggregates act mainly as filler material, providing bulk and volume to the concrete, while cement paste acts as the binder holding them together.

q: 14. Minimum number of days required for curing fresh laid concrete under normal atmospheric condition is
explain: Under normal atmospheric conditions, a minimum curing period of 7 days is generally specified to allow adequate hydration and strength gain of concrete.

q: 15. Volume of coarse aggregate required to make 100m3 of 1:2:4 concrete is
explain: For a 1:2:4 mix (7 parts total, with dry volume factor ~1.54-1.55), the coarse aggregate proportion (4/7) of the total dry volume works out to approximately 84m3 for 100m3 of finished concrete.

q: 16. In the manufacture of cement, the dry or wet mixture of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt at a temperature between
explain: In the kiln, the raw mixture of calcareous (limestone) and argillaceous (clay) materials is burnt at very high temperatures of about 1500°C to 1600°C to form clinker.

q: 17. The chemical ingredient of cement which provides quick setting property to the cement is
explain: Alumina in cement lowers the clinkering temperature and imparts quick setting properties, though excess alumina can weaken the cement.

q: 18. The gypsum is added to the cement for
options: providing high strength to the cement
controlling the initial setting time of cement
lowering the initial setting time of cement
explain: Gypsum is added during grinding of clinker specifically to retard/control the initial setting time of cement, preventing flash setting caused by tricalcium aluminate.

q: 19. Which of the following ingredient of cement when added in excess quantity, caused the cement to set slowly?
explain: Excess silica in cement makes the cement set slowly, as it increases the proportion of dicalcium silicate which hydrates and hardens slowly.

q: 20. Lime when added in excess quantity
options: caused the cement to expand and disintegrate
lowers the clinkering temperature of cement
explain: Excess free lime in cement remains uncombined, and upon hydration it expands, causing the cement to become unsound and disintegrate.

q: 21. After the final grinding, the cement is sieved thought IS sieve number
explain: IS sieve No. 9 (90 micron) is used to check the fineness of finely ground cement after the grinding process is complete.

q: 22. Efflorescence in cement is caused due to the excess of
explain: Excess alkalies in cement react with moisture and carbon dioxide, migrating to the surface and crystallizing as a white efflorescence deposit.

q: 23. The presence of tricalcium silicate in cement
options: offers high resistance to sulphate attack
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) hydrates and hardens rapidly, contributing to early strength gain, but it generates high heat of hydration and offers low sulphate resistance.

q: 24. The presence of dicalcium silicate in cement
options: has more resistance to sulphate attack
explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly, generates less heat of hydration, and provides better resistance to sulphate attack, so all three statements apply.

q: 25. The tricalcium aluminate in cement has the property of
options: generating large amount of heat hydration
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts very fast with water, is chiefly responsible for the initial set, and releases a large amount of heat of hydration.

q: 26. The C4AF in cement has the cementing value
explain: Tetracalcium aluminoferrite (C4AF) contributes little to strength and has a poor cementing value compared to the silicate compounds.

q: 27. High percentage of tricalcium silicate and low percentage of dicalcium silicate in cement results in
explain: A higher proportion of fast-hydrating C3S relative to slow-hydrating C2S leads to rapid hardening, high early strength, and higher heat of hydration, all together.

q: 28. The sum of the percentage of tricalcium silicate and dicalcium silicate for Portland cement varies from
explain: The two calcium silicate compounds (C3S and C2S) together typically make up about 70% to 80% of ordinary Portland cement's composition, as they are the primary strength-giving compounds.

q: 29. The cement, widely used in retaining walls, is
explain: Retaining walls are mass concrete structures where controlling heat of hydration to avoid thermal cracking is important, so low heat cement is preferred.

q: 30. Which of the following cements is expected to have the highest compressive strength after 3 days?
explain: High alumina cement gains strength extremely rapidly, achieving very high compressive strength within the first few days, higher than other cement types.

q: 31. In the manufacture of pozzolana cement, the amount of pozzolana material added to ordinary Portland cement clinkers is about
explain: Portland pozzolana cement is manufactured by blending about 30% pozzolanic material with ordinary Portland cement clinker.

q: 32. The hardening is the phenomenon by virtue of which
options: the cement does not undergo large change in volume when treated with water
the plastic cement paste changes into hard mass
the cement paste sets and develops strength
explain: Hardening refers to the process where the cement paste, after setting, continues to gain strength over time through ongoing hydration.

q: 33. The phenomenon by virtue of which the cement does not undergo large change in volume when treated with water, is known as
explain: Soundness refers to cement's ability to not undergo excessive volume change (expansion) after setting when exposed to water, which prevents cracking.

q: 34. The compressive strength of an ordinary Portland cement (1: 3 cement mortar cube) after 7 days test should not be less than
explain: As per IS specifications, a 1:3 cement-sand mortar cube of ordinary Portland cement must achieve a minimum compressive strength of 17.5 N/mm² after 7 days.

q: 35. The length of Vicat plunger in Vicat's apparatus varies from
explain: The Vicat plunger used for the standard consistency test has a length specified between 40mm and 50mm as per standard apparatus dimensions.

q: 36. The percentage of water for making a cement paste of normal consistency varies from
explain: The standard consistency of cement paste, determined by the Vicat apparatus, is typically achieved with water content in the range of about 35% to 50% by weight of cement.

q: 37. To perform the initial setting time test, the water is added to the cement at the rate of .... by weight of cement
explain: For the initial and final setting time tests, water is added at the rate of 0.85 times the water needed for standard consistency (P), i.e., 0.85P, as per IS code.

q: 38. To perform the compressive strength test of cement, water is added at the rate of
explain: For the compressive strength test of cement mortar, the water content used is (P/4 + 3%) of the combined weight of cement and sand, as specified by IS code, matching option c's form (P + 3% of water).

q: 39. The cubes of cement prepared for compressive strength they should be kept at a temperature of ............ in an atmosphere of at least 90% relative humidity for 24 hours.
explain: As per IS standards, cement cubes must be kept at a temperature of 27°C ± 2°C in an atmosphere of at least 90% relative humidity for 24 hours before demoulding.

q: 40. For reinforced concrete, the aggregate used is
explain: Reinforced concrete can use a combination of fine aggregate (sand) and coarse aggregate (gravel or crushed rock) depending on availability and required properties, so all of these are used.

q: 41. Maturity of concrete means
options: sum of product of temperature and time
explain: Maturity of concrete is a concept defined as the sum of the products of curing temperature and time, used to estimate strength development.

q: 42. The aggregate which pass through 75 mm IS sieve and entirely retain on 4.75 mm IS sieve is known as
explain: Aggregate passing 75mm sieve but retained on 4.75mm sieve is classified as coarse aggregate as per standard aggregate size classification.

q: 43. The maximum particle size of coarse aggregate is
explain: By standard classification, coarse aggregate can have particle sizes up to a maximum of 75mm, beyond which it is termed cyclopean aggregate.

q: 44. The aggregate which pass through 4.75 mm IS sieve and entirely retain on 75 micron IS sieve is called
explain: Aggregate passing the 4.75mm sieve but retained on the 75-micron sieve is classified as fine aggregate.

q: 45. The aggregates of ......shape have minimum voids.
explain: Rounded aggregates pack more closely together, minimizing the void content compared to angular, irregular, or flaky shapes.

q: 46. The aggregates of ...........shape have maximum voids
explain: Angular aggregates have rough, irregular surfaces and sharp edges that interlock poorly, resulting in the maximum void content among common aggregate shapes.

q: 47. The aggregate is said to be flaky when
options: its least dimension is three-fifth of its mean dimension
its least dimension is equal to its mean dimension
its length is equal to its mean dimension
its length is equal to 1.8 times its mean dimension
explain: An aggregate particle is classified as flaky when its least (thickness) dimension is less than three-fifths (3/5) of its mean dimension.

q: 48. Bulk specific gravity of an aggregate is defined as
options: the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, excluding the natural pores in the aggregate particles
the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, including the natural pores in the aggregate particles
the weight of aggregate required to fill a container of unit volume
the difference in weight of the aggregate in saturated surface dry condition and in moist condition
explain: Bulk specific gravity is defined as the weight of oven-dry aggregate divided by its total (bulk) volume, which includes the natural pores within the particles.

q: 49. The apparent specific gravity of an aggregate is defined as
options: the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, excluding the natural pores in the aggregate particles
the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, excluding the natural process in the aggregate particles
the weight of aggregate required to fill a container of unit volume
the difference in weight of the aggregate in saturated surface dry condition and in moist condition
explain: Apparent specific gravity is the weight of oven-dry aggregate divided by its absolute (solid) volume, excluding the natural pores within the particles.

q: 50. An aggregate which may contain some moisture in the pores but having dry surface is known as
explain: Saturated surface dry (SSD) aggregate has its internal pores filled or partially filled with water, but its outer surface is dry, matching this description.

q: 51. An aggregate having all the pores filled with water but having dry surface is called
explain: This is precisely the definition of saturated surface dry (SSD) aggregate: pores fully saturated with water while the outer surface remains dry.

q: 52. A moist aggregate is one
options: whose all the pores are filled with water and also having its surface wet
whose all the pores are filled with water but having its surface dry
which do not contain any moisture in the pores but having dry surface
which may contain some moisture in the pores but having dry surface
explain: A moist aggregate has all its pores filled with water and additionally carries free water on its surface, making the surface wet.

q: 53. The resistance of an aggregate to compressive forces is known as
explain: The crushing value test measures the resistance of aggregate to crushing under a gradually applied compressive load.

q: 54. The resistance of an aggregate to wear is known as
explain: The abrasion value indicates the aggregate's resistance to surface wear caused by rubbing or grinding action, such as traffic wear on road surfaces.

q: 55. The resistance of an aggregate to the effect of hydration of cement and weather is called
explain: Soundness of an aggregate refers to its ability to resist volume changes due to weathering action, freezing-thawing, and chemical reactions such as those from cement hydration.

q: 56. The ratio of the volume of moist sand to the volume of dry sand is known as
explain: The bulking factor is the ratio of the volume of moist (bulked) sand to the volume of the same sand in dry condition, reflecting the increase in volume due to moisture films between particles.

q: 57. The rule of water cement ratio was established by
explain: The water-cement ratio law, relating strength of concrete inversely to the water-cement ratio, was established by Duff Abrams in 1918.

q: 58. Water-cement ratio is, usually, expressed in
options: liters of water required per bag of cement
liters of water required per kg of cement
explain: Water-cement ratio can be conveniently expressed in either liters of water per bag of cement or liters of water per kg of cement, since both are equivalent ways of expressing the same ratio.

q: 59. The internal friction between the ingredients of concrete is minimized by
explain: Internal friction in a concrete mix can be reduced through several means together: using coarser aggregates, adding more water for lubrication, and reducing surface area/texture of particles, hence all of these contribute.

q: 60. The slump test of concrete is used to measure its
explain: The slump test primarily measures the consistency (a measure of wetness/workability) of fresh concrete by observing how much it settles after removing the slump cone.

q: 61. The test conducted in the laboratory on the specimen made out of trial concrete mix is called
explain: A preliminary test is conducted in the laboratory on trial mixes before actual construction to determine and verify the proportions needed to achieve the required strength.

q: 62. If 30 % excess water is added, the strength of concrete is reduced by
explain: Excess water disproportionately weakens concrete strength; adding 30% excess water can reduce the resulting strength by as much as 50%, according to established water-cement ratio relationships.

q: 63. The maximum quantity of aggregate per 50 kg of cement should not exceed
explain: As per general guidelines, the total quantity of aggregate (fine plus coarse) used per 50kg bag of cement should not exceed about 450kg for good quality concrete.

q: 64. The concrete in which no preliminary tests are performed for designing the mix is called
explain: Ordinary (nominal mix) concrete is proportioned using fixed ratios (e.g., 1:2:4) without conducting preliminary trial mix tests, unlike controlled/design mix concrete.

q: 65. For reinforced cement concrete lintels and slabs, the nominal size of coarse aggregate should not exceed
explain: For thin reinforced sections like lintels and slabs, a smaller nominal aggregate size (15mm) is used to allow proper flow around closely spaced reinforcement.

q: 66. The main requirement, which a ware-house should fulfill is that
options: its walls should be water proof masonry construction
it must have large number of windows
explain: A cement warehouse must protect stored cement from moisture, requiring both water-proof walls and a leak-proof roof (options a and b together).

q: 67. The term 'ware-house pack' means
options: pressure compaction of bags in lower layers
pressure exertion of bags on upper layers
explain: 'Warehouse pack' refers to the phenomenon where cement bags stored in lower layers get compacted due to the pressure of bags stacked above them.

q: 68. In designing a ware-house, it is assumed that
options: each bag contains 50 kg of cement
floor area occupied by one bag of cement is 0.3 m2
height of each cement bag containing 35 liters of cement is 0.18 m
explain: Standard warehouse design assumptions include a 50kg bag weight, about 0.3m² floor area per bag, and about 0.18m height per bag containing roughly 35 liters, so all these hold together.

q: 69. The importance of batching is to obtain
explain: Accurate batching of ingredients ensures the desired mix proportions, which in turn affects and helps achieve strength, workability, and durability all together.

q: 70. The mixer, which produces a steady stream of concrete as long as it is in operation, is known as
explain: A continuous mixer feeds materials in continuously and discharges a steady, uninterrupted stream of mixed concrete for as long as it operates, unlike batch mixers which discharge in batches.

q: 71. For continuous transportation of concrete, the method used is
options: transport of concrete by wheel barrows
transport of concrete by wheel barrows
transport of concrete by belt concrete conveyors
explain: Belt conveyors provide a continuous, uninterrupted method of transporting concrete over distances, unlike wheel barrows or pumps used for other applications.

q: 72. In transportation of concrete by pumps
options: the slump should not be less than 50 mm and more than 80mm
the water cement ratio should remain between 0.5 to 0.65
the number of bends in a pipe line should be as small as possible
explain: Successful pumping of concrete requires appropriate slump range, controlled water-cement ratio, and minimizing pipeline bends to reduce friction losses, so all conditions apply together.

q: 73. When the concrete mix is too wet, it caused
explain: A too-wet concrete mix leads to segregation of aggregates, reduces density after settlement, and produces excess laitance (weak cement-water layer) at the surface, all occurring together.

q: 74. The object of compaction is to
options: ensure intimate contact between the concrete and the surface of reinforcement
explain: Compaction serves multiple purposes simultaneously: removing entrapped air, achieving maximum density, and ensuring the concrete surrounds reinforcement completely.

q: 75. For compacting large sections of mass concrete in structures, the types of vibrator used is
explain: Internal (needle) vibrators are inserted directly into the concrete mass and are best suited for compacting large sections of mass concrete.

q: 76. For compacting plain concrete or one-way reinforced concrete floors, the vibrator used is
explain: Screed vibrators are mounted on a screed board and are ideal for compacting relatively thin, flat sections like plain concrete or one-way reinforced floors.

q: 77. After the curing of 28 days, the concrete gains strength upto (As per IS)
explain: By IS convention, 28-day cured concrete is considered to have gained 100% of its designated characteristic (design) strength, though it continues to gain further strength beyond 28 days.

q: 78. In concrete walls, construction joints should be provided at the
explain: Construction joints in walls are conveniently located at floor levels, lintel soffit levels, and window sill levels, as these are natural break points in the wall's structural continuity.

q: 79. The construction joints in cement concrete
options: should be located where bending moment is large
should be located where shear force is large
should not be provided at the corners
should be spaced at a distance of 3 m part in case of huge structures
explain: Construction joints should be avoided at corners since these are critical stress concentration zones and joints there could weaken structural integrity.

q: 80. The construction joints are generally provided in concrete
explain: Construction joints are a common feature across many types of concrete structures including roads, retaining walls, and tunnel linings, wherever concreting must be done in stages.
